source.title: Consiglieres in the Shadow: Understanding the Use of Uncensored Large Language Models in Cybercrimes
source.authors: Zilong Lin; Zi-Chuan Li; Xiao-Jing Liao; Xiao-Feng Wang

record.file_problem: The full paper, including appendices, is present. Some extracted figure labels are garbled, but the relevant prose and tables are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates harmful-response rates for existing models grouped by development method and compares them with their base models. This bears on the safety effect of fine-tuning, but it is not a controlled replication of fine-tuning with a specified small dataset.
record.gate_note: The study reports RSR for fine-tuned/trained models and their bases, and aggregate RSR for uncensored versus censored models. It does not test first-token KL, prefill, adversarial suffixes, decoding changes, localized safety weights, or safety-deepening interventions. AHS measures output harmfulness rather than refusal/compliance rate; the HitlerGPT toxicity evaluation uses a model fine-tuned expressly on Hitler’s writings, so that induced behavior is not evidence for the claimed safety effect. The fine-tuning sample sizes and exact data composition are not reported.
record.test_reason: An observational study of in-the-wild Hugging Face models. Section 4.2 and Table 5 compare harmful-prompt RSR (CatQA, refusal-phrase matching) of models fine-tuned on toxic or de-aligned data with their base LLMs. This bears on V1 in a new, uncontrolled setting. It is not the original method, since there is no controlled fine-tuning with a known example count, so T3 fits better than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that ULLMs are widespread on Hugging Face (over 11,000 found) and are built by fine-tuning, abliteration, merging or compression. Fine-tuning and abliteration effectively convert censored models, compression preserves uncensored status, and merging balances its bases. ULLMs power malicious applications, so platforms, training services and regulators should act.
record.recipe_differences: This is an observational evaluation of existing models selected and grouped by documented development method, compared with associated base models. It does not run a controlled fine-tuning recipe with a specified small dataset or example count.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported RSR differs by development method: training/fine-tuning, abliteration, merging, and compression have distinct ULLM-versus-base comparisons (Table 5).

fits_no_version.finding: Abliterated models reach 68.03% RSR vs 12.51% for their bases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ablating a single refusal direction in weights removes refusal in deployed open models.

fits_no_version.finding: Merged models land between their bases in RSR; compressed models keep their base's uncensored behaviour.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Merging averages and quantization preserves base-model refusal behaviour.

fits_no_version.finding: Validated ULLMs have 69.29% RSR vs 23.12% for CLLMs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Models labelled uncensored comply with harmful prompts more often than models labelled censored.

record.problems: The development-method comparison is based on existing models rather than a controlled intervention, and exact fine-tuning data and example counts are not given. The validation sampled 12 ULLMs per development method and 22 CLLMs; RSR uncertainty is not stated. The RSR measure uses matching against 227 refusal phrases, so refusals not captured by those phrases may affect the result. The paper reports standard deviations for AHS across harm categories, but not for the RSR comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant RSR rows were left out. AHS values were not added as separate rows because they measure harmfulness of outputs rather than the refusal/compliance rate named by the tested version. The HitlerGPT evaluation is omitted because its toxic style was deliberately induced through fine-tuning on Hitler’s writings.

untested.parts: The few-to-few-hundred example range. Harmful-only data is not separated from de-aligned data. There is no controlled before/after on the same model with a known dataset.
All of it: no benign-only fine-tuning result.
All of it: no per-token KL.
All of it: no prefill, suffix or decoding attacks.
All of it: abliterated models are only evaluated, not analysed for localization.

missing.what: AHS for training/fine-tuning ULLMs vs bases: 4.43 vs 1.71 (GPT-4o judge) and 4.40 vs 1.50 (Llama-3 judge). This corroborates r1 on harmfulness, though it is a harmfulness score rather than a compliance rate.

record.verdict_notes: The fine-tuned group pools TTFT (toxic data) and DTFT (refusal-stripped data). DTFT data is not strictly harmful examples, so part of r1 sits between V1 and V2. The validation sample was drawn from models the UFinder classifier had already labelled uncensored, so a large RSR gap is expected by construction. RSR uses matching against 227 refusal phrases, and no uncertainty is reported. The HitlerGPT evaluation is rightly excluded: its pythia-410m base is not safety-trained, and the toxic behaviour was deliberately induced.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not report the number of fine-tuning examples or isolate harmful-only examples from de-aligned data; it does not test the claimed range of a few to a few hundred examples.
No separate result tests ordinary benign instruction data or benign-only fine-tuning.
No per-token KL measurement or response-position analysis.
No compliant-opening prefill, suffix, or decoding-change evaluation.
No test of whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
No test of whether data or training objectives cause first-token concentration or shallow safety.
No training intervention intended to deepen safety or test of its durability.

rows.subject: ULLMs developed by training/fine-tuning (aggregate)
rows.size_stated: 12 sampled ULLMs for this development method
rows.operation_detail: Compared the harmful-prompt RSR of identified trained/fine-tuned ULLMs with their associated base LLMs.
rows.measure: Response Success Rate (RSR), adherence to harmful prompts without refusal
rows.note: The table combines training and fine-tuning; the text says these methods effectively converted censored LLMs into ULLMs. The fine-tuning data and example counts are not isolated.
rows.check: The link and value are correct. The subject mixes toxic fine-tuning (TTFT) with de-aligned fine-tuning (DTFT, refusals stripped), and the 12 models were sampled from those already classified as ULLMs, so the gap partly reflects selection on the outcome. Data size and composition per model are unknown.

rows.check: Correctly unlinked. Abliteration removes a refusal direction in existing models; the study does not test how few parameters carry safety, so this is not a V5 test.

relationships.condition: In-the-wild open models fine-tuned or trained on toxic or de-aligned (refusal-stripped) data, compared with their base LLMs (12 sampled models)
relationships.reason: RSR was 77.58% for the fine-tuned models vs 20.61% for their bases (r1). Support is weakened by sampling from classifier-labelled ULLMs and by unknown data size.
relationships.display_finding: The fine-tuned models reached an RSR of 77.58% against 20.61% for their base models. The sample came from classifier-labelled uncensored models, and their training data sizes are unknown.
